parts:
I just figured I'd make a new post to let people know ( who don't already know ) that there's a very nice discussion of non-informative /locally uniform priors on page 21 and 25-31 of Box and Tiao. Ben, if you read that, it explains how the  joint prior in adl_gibbs.pdf  becomes 1/sigma. It turns out that the marginal priors for beta and lambda that result in that joint prior are called locally uniform priors.  ( but better to read that than to listen to my babblings ).  Not that the joint prior is adl_gibbs.pdf is necessarily a good joint prior but it does hold to the idea that the priors for all three parameters ( sigma, beta, and lambda ) be locally uniform.

I think the discussion in Box and Tiao may also be related to what Michael said about Hamiltonian dynamics having problems when a parameter in the model has mass near infinity. But I need to read adl_gibbs.pdf in detail
before I say or think any more on that. I'll be in touch and thanks to everyone for their great help.
